Chapter 2

Arriving in Freiburg, Germany

Airport

Basel–Mulhouse Airport

1. Arrival by bus — Freiburg Shuttle bus service

This is a shuttle bus from the airport directly to Freiburg main station (55 mins). The bus is scheduled every 1 hour.

Duration: around 1 hourCost: starts from 25€
Shuttle bus schedule
Airport

Frankfurt Airport

1. Arrival by train

From Frankfurt Flughafen Fernbf take a train (ICE – direct ride) to Freiburg (Breisgau) Hbf (direction to Basel SBB).

Duration: about 2 h 20 minsCost: from 28€

The price is not fixed, rises closer to the date.

2. Arrival by bus (Flixbus)

From Frankfurt Main Airport P36 to Freiburg (Breisgau) Hbf.

Duration: from 3 h 50 minsCost: from 15€

The price is not fixed, rises closer to the date.

Airport

Munich Airport

1. Arrival by train

First take a bus to Munchen Flughafen, Airport Center (MAC) (7 mins). Then from Munchen Flughafen Terminal take S-Bahn to Munchen Hbf (45 mins). From Munchen Hbf take ICE train to Freiburg (Breisgau) Hbf (4 hours).

Duration: from 5 h 10 minsCost: from 60€

The price is not fixed, rises closer to the date.

Important
  1. All travel durations and prices are approximate. Only the time spent in transit is considered, excluding walking to transportation and waiting.
  2. Delays in transportation, which are common in Germany, were not taken into account. Trains and buses often run late, occasionally may not reach their final destination, and platforms may be changed at the very last minutes. Please be cautious.
Chapter 3

Public Transport in Freiburg

Moving inside Freiburg is pretty easy. The transport company in Freiburg is the VAG.

3.1Trams (Straßenbahn)

The tram is the primary mode of transportation within Freiburg and offers a delightful way to explore the city's charming streets. We highly recommend trying it out at least once during your stay. Freiburg has five tram lines, conveniently numbered from 1 to 5 and distinguished by different colors. These tram lines cover extensive areas, providing easy access to various destinations throughout the city.

The schedules can be found here or in Google Maps:

  • vag-freiburg.de — Tram & bus schedules (also available in the VAG Application or in Google Maps)
Important — Tram working hours

Monday to Friday: 5:30 am – 12:30 am (midnight). However, on the nights between Friday and Saturday, as well as Saturday and Sunday, and holidays, trams operate 24/7.

Buses: You can find the exact schedule of the buses here:

  • vag-freiburg.de — Bus schedules

3.2.3 Freiburg zones

Freiburg is divided into 3 zones: A, B & C. Price of the ticket is different for each zone. Almost all the places you'd need are included in the first zone A. However, if you want to extend your discoveries a bit further, you would need another ticket.

A B C

3.3Tickets

Fare evasion notice

Having a valid ticket is essential when using public transport in Germany. Fare evasion can result in a 60€ fine!

3.3.1 Tickets Buying

Tickets can be purchased from ticket machines located at many tram stations or from inside the tram itself. Alternatively, you can buy tickets online. When riding the tram, remember to validate your ticket by stamping it in the designated box. However, if you're taking the bus, there are no ticket machines available. In this case, you can purchase your ticket directly from the bus driver (either an Einzelfahrt Ticket or a 24-hour ticket) or buy it online. Please note that to buy tickets online, you will need to download the VAG application. For a list of stations with ticket machines, you can visit the following link:

  • vag-freiburg.de — Ticket machine locations

3.3.2 Tickets Explained

Single Ticket (Einzelfahrschein)

The single ticket is suitable if you infrequently use the bus or tram. It is valid for a single trip with a specific destination. Transfers are allowed as long as they are in the same direction; however, returning on the same ticket is not permitted.

Single Ticket pricing by zone level

View on vag-freiburg.de

Short distance Ticket (Kurzstrecke)

For those who are spontaneous, there is a ticket option available that allows travel for up to 3 stations on either the tram or bus. Transfers are allowed within a maximum trip duration of 20 minutes.

Cost: 1.90€

View on vag-freiburg.de

2x4 Ticket (2x4-FahrtenKarte)

This ticket option is akin to purchasing 8 single tickets together, with some discount applied to the total price. Each ticket functions as a regular single ticket, allowing you to travel to a specific destination. Transfers are permitted during the journey; however, using the ticket to travel back in the opposite direction is not allowed. Additionally, it's important to note that this ticket can be used by multiple people.

2x4 Ticket pricing by zone level

122.50€1

Day ticket (Regio24)

This ticket provides unlimited travel for 24 hours starting from the time of purchase or activation. It can be used for multiple trips and to various destinations. You have the freedom to ride the bus, train, and light rail as frequently as you wish throughout the entire day.

3.3.3Cool tickets and other means of transportation

Student special

For students enrolled at Albert Ludwigs University, public transportation within Freiburg is free of charge after 19:00 every day, as well as on Sundays and public holidays. To take advantage of this benefit, you will need to carry your Unicard (university ID card) and the certificate of enrollment with you during your ride. In addition to these documents, you will also need to obtain the free night pass. You can order your free night pass by visiting the following link:

Order your free night pass

Deutschland-Ticket

Introducing the Deutschland-Ticket (D-Ticket), a convenient way to travel across Germany. For just 63 euros per month, you can enjoy unlimited travel on all public transportation. The D-Ticket is now available for purchase online, through the app, and at DB travel centers.

With the Deutschland-Ticket, you have access to local trains like RB, RE, S-Bahn trains, as well as public transport options such as buses, trams, and underground trains throughout Germany. It's important to note that the D-Ticket is not valid on IC, EC, ICE trains, or other long-distance transportation providers like FlixTrain. For more information follow this link:

bahn.de — Deutschland-Ticket
Bikes renting

Explore the beauty of Freiburg by bike, which is the preferred mode of transportation for residents, especially students. Through a partnership between Frelo, a bike rental company affiliated with nextbike, and the University of Freiburg, students can ride bikes for free as long as each trip is within a 30-minute duration. To benefit from this offer, you can return the bike to a station within 30 minutes and then in 10 minutes to take a new one for another free 30-minute ride. Otherwise, 30 extra mins cost 1€.

Simply register with your university email.

frelo-freiburg.de

Chapter 4

Living in Germany

4.1.1The currency

The official currency of Germany is the Euro. If you are visiting from a country with a different currency, it's important to note that you will need to exchange your currency for Euros in order to make purchases. Without Euros, you won't be able to buy anything. Alternatively, you can use your debit or credit card, which will be charged for your expenses during your stay in Germany.

germany-visa.org — Living in Germany

4.1.2Germans love their rules

It's the stereotypical opinion, but Germans are a rule loving people. They have written and unwritten laws which they adhere to religiously. If you happen to break a rule, don't expect to be excused easily. For instance, crossing the street against a red pedestrian light (jaywalking) may earn you disapproving looks or even a scolding from a passerby. It's important to familiarize yourself with the rules and regulations in your new home, ensuring that you are aware of what is permissible and what is not. By staying informed, you can navigate your new environment with respect for the local norms and regulations.

4.1.3Bad customer service

In contrast to the saying "the customer is king" that prevails in some places, you might be surprised by the level of customer service in Germany. Germans are often perceived as not providing exceptional customer service, or at least not to the extent that many Americans, Canadians, and other Europeans are used to.

4.1.4Good public transport

In Germany, trams and buses are known for their punctuality and cleanliness. Public transportation is widely utilized and offers an excellent experience. The emphasis on order and timeliness is highly valued, ensuring that you will have a positive and efficient journey when using public transport.

4.1.5Cities built for bikes

Freiburg's road infrastructure is designed to accommodate various modes of transportation. The roads are pedestrian-friendly, but most importantly, they are bicycle-friendly. Using a bicycle will likely be the most cost-effective mode of transportation. Here, you will find that almost all roads feature dedicated bike lanes, and cyclists are a common sight throughout the town.

4.1.6Recycling friendly

In Germany, maintaining order extends to waste management. You will encounter separate bins for different types of garbage, and recycling has designated times. Germany's strong commitment to environmental sustainability means it's important to familiarize yourself with recycling practices and proper sorting of materials when you move there.

4.1.7Everything closes down on Sunday

It may sound unusual, but it is true that all stores in Germany are closed on Saturday evenings and do not reopen until Monday morning. However, there are a few exceptions. Some bakeries open for a short period in the morning, and there are a limited number of emergency pharmacies that remain open. The only supermarket that operates 365 days a year is the "Supermarkt am Bahnhof," located in the underground area of the train station. This supermarket also closes at midnight and reopens at 06:00 hours. It's important to plan your shopping accordingly, keeping in mind the store closures during the weekend.

Chapter 6

WiFi Eduroam

WLAN at Freiburg University

The University IT Service offers WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network) in almost every University building.

WLAN

In order to access the University's WLAN via eduroam, you need a portable device, such as a laptop or phone, a valid Uni-Account, as well as an eduroam-password (RAS password), which you can set up in myAccount.

We could provide temporary wifi passwords. Please just ask.
